svg.title: EternalWeb in action
svg.desc: A county flood-gauge page changes and then returns 404 at the same URL. EternalWeb names the page by its content instead: a BLAKE3 content address, which changes completely when one character changes and rejects edited bytes. An archivist signs the address with Ed25519; the signature fails on the edited page. Each version keeps its own address, so the March readings survive the removal. Peer replication is shown as the roadmap design. Reputation and curation scores come from the library, and the closing list separates what works today from what is next.

g.text: A URL NAMES A PLACE, NOT A THING
places change; what they pointed to disappears
Readings every 15 minutes since 1998, published by the county
Historical data is no longer available.
the address never changed. what it pointed to did.
NAME IT BY WHAT IT IS
the address is a fingerprint of the bytes themselves (BLAKE3, CIDv1)
49 of 59 characters change · a different thing gets a different name
an archivist's Ed25519 signature over the address
✗ copied onto the edited page: rejected
A REMOVAL IS A NEW VERSION, NOT AN ERASURE
each version keeps its own address
Historical data is no longer available.
bafkr4icgbnkhx2htl7rxy… still returns the March readings, byte for byte
the design: archives replicate across peers, so no single server decides what survives
designed, not built: libp2p replication is on the roadmap. Today an archive lives in the local store of the node that made it.
credit for archiving, hosting and curating; no speculative coin
CURATION OF THE MARCH ARCHIVE · quality score
upvotes ÷ (upvotes + downvotes) · flags are counted separately
WHAT WORKS TODAY, AND WHAT'S NEXT
name what you keep by what it is, not where it lives
